reason: R0 and R1 form a resistive link/coupling between VOUT1 and VOUT2 through net5; removing one of them typically just reduces that cross-coupling rather than destroying the core NMOS transconductor behavior. Caveat: if the R0–R1 network is intentionally providing common-mode feedback or output balancing, deleting it will degrade symmetry/CMRR and may shift output common-mode.

Similarly, R1 is part of the same output-to-net5 coupling network; removing it breaks the resistive averaging node net5 while the two NMOS devices can still function as separate gain paths. Caveat: if net5 is required to set the PMOS gates to a stable bias (via averaging VOUT1/VOUT2), removing R1 can make net5 depend only on the remaining connection and change biasing.
impact_estimate: Low-to-medium (affects net5 definition and output balance)

reason: M10 is a PMOS load/pull-up for the VOUT1 branch; if you keep M11 and/or you have an external load/bias on VOUT1, the circuit can still operate conceptually as a differential pair with degraded gain/swing on that side. Caveat: without M10, VOUT1 may lose its active load, reducing gain substantially and potentially leaving VOUT1 unable to pull up, so this is only “safe” if another load exists.
impact_estimate: Medium (keeps basic operation but degrades gain/swing on VOUT1)
